title: Microsoft Purview classifiers: what recognises sensitive content, and who controls it?
summary: The page passes: its admin paths, commands, roles, sample requirements and scan limits are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should acknowledge differing education licensing guidance and endpoint rescan behaviour, and cite the endpoint page supporting policy evaluation.

claims.claim: Classifiers identify sensitive content using rules or models for policies and labels.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview classifiers help administrators identify sensitive content so they can protect and manage it.

claims.claim: The Classifiers page brings classification types together for discovery, creation, inspection and management.
claims.quote: The Classifiers page brings classification types together in one experience where you can discover, create, inspect, and manage classifiers.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: The page shows how many policies use each classifier.
claims.quote: You can also see how many policies use a classifier and inspect those dependencies before changing it.

claims.claim: The new Classifiers experience is in preview.
claims.quote: The new Classifiers experience in Microsoft Purview is in preview

claims.claim: The new experience runs alongside existing classification experiences.
claims.quote: is available alongside the existing classification experiences.

claims.claim: Classifier changes in either experience appear in the other.
claims.quote: Classifiers you create, edit, or delete in either experience are reflected in the other.

claims.claim: Sensitive information types identify patterns such as social security, credit card and bank account numbers.
claims.quote: Sensitive information types (SITs) identify content that matches patterns of sensitive information, such as social security, credit card, or bank account numbers.

claims.claim: Named entities use dictionaries and patterns to detect names, addresses, and medical terms and conditions.
claims.quote: Named entities are sensitive information types that use dictionaries and patterns to detect person names, physical addresses, and medical terms and conditions.

claims.claim: Exact data match recognises exact values.
claims.quote: Exact data match identifies sensitive content by matching exact values.

claims.claim: Trainable classifiers learn content categories from examples rather than pattern matching.
claims.quote: This categorization method is well suited to content that can't be easily identified using either the manual or automated pattern-matching methods. A classifier learns how to identify a type of content by looking at hundreds of examples of the content you want to detect.

claims.claim: Credential classifiers detect credentials from supported services and environments.
claims.quote: The All credentials sensitive information type groups individual credential types to detect credentials from supported services and environments.

claims.claim: Document fingerprinting recognises variations of a template.
claims.quote: Document fingerprinting recognizes content that is a variation of a template.

claims.claim: Microsoft provides pretrained trainable classifiers ready to use.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview provides pretrained trainable classifiers that are ready to use.

claims.claim: Administrators can create custom trainable classifiers from content samples.
claims.quote: You can also create custom trainable classifiers by providing samples of the content you want to recognize.

claims.claim: Training requires at least 50 positive samples.
claims.quote: You need at least 50 positive samples (up to 500)

claims.claim: Training accepts up to 500 positive samples.
claims.quote: You need at least 50 positive samples (up to 500)

claims.claim: Training requires at least 150 negative samples.
claims.quote: at least 150 negative samples (up to 1,500) to train a classifier.

claims.claim: Training accepts up to 1,500 negative samples.
claims.quote: at least 150 negative samples (up to 1,500) to train a classifier.

claims.quote: Place the positive and negative seed content in separate SharePoint folders.

claims.claim: On-demand classification scans historical files at rest in SharePoint, OneDrive and endpoints.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview on-demand classification identifies and classifies sensitive content in historical data stored in SharePoint, OneDrive, and endpoints.

claims.claim: On-demand classification includes files never classified.
claims.quote: files that are never classified

claims.claim: On-demand classification includes files not modified for a long time.
claims.quote: On-demand classification extends the classification capabilities to files that aren't classified or modified for a long time

claims.claim: On-demand classification updates classification results.
claims.quote: On-demand classification updates classification results

claims.quote:
Use classifiers as a condition for:

Communication compliance supports Microsoft provided trainable classifiers only.
Sensitivity label conditions.
Data loss prevention

claims.claim: Classifiers can be used in sensitivity label conditions.
claims.quote: Sensitivity label conditions. (See Automatically apply a sensitivity label to Microsoft 365 data)

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Communication compliance supports Microsoft provided trainable classifiers, not custom ones.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance supports the use of the Microsoft provided trainable classifiers only. Custom trainable classifiers aren't supported.

claims.where: Why it matters: scanned-file policy evaluation
claims.claim: Scanned files are evaluated against DLP, Information Protection, Data Lifecycle Management and Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: Files are evaluated against DLP, Microsoft Information Protection (MIP), data lifecycle management (DLM), and insider risk management (IRM) policies simultaneously.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/on-demand-classification-endpoints to sources: it supports endpoint policy evaluation; the existing on-demand-classification citation states this under SharePoint and OneDrive considerations.

claims.claim: The service description lists E5/A5/G5, Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW, Defender + Purview Suite FLW, and E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance for trainable-classifier retention auto-apply.

claims.claim: On-demand classification uses pay-as-you-go billing, per-user licensing, or both.
claims.quote: This feature uses pay-as-you-go billing or per-user licensing for Microsoft Purview capabilities or both.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing uses an Azure subscription associated with the tenant.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: The on-demand classification pay-as-you-go meter is assets classified per scan.
claims.quote: On-demand classification | Applies when you run a scan to identify and classify sensitive content in data stored in SharePoint and OneDrive | Asset, based on the number classified per scan

claims.claim: Skipped items or locations can make the final billed amount lower than the estimate.
claims.quote: The actual billed amount may be lower than the estimated cost if some items or locations are skipped during the scan.

claims.claim: Empty files can be excluded to avoid unnecessary billing.
claims.quote: Items can be skipped if they are empty files (excluded to avoid unnecessary billing)

claims.claim: Cancelling a scan can result in skipped items and a lower bill.
claims.quote: Items can be skipped if they are empty files (excluded to avoid unnecessary billing), if the scan is canceled, or if the subscription expires before completion.

claims.claim: Scan cost follows the total number of files scanned.
claims.quote: Scan cost is determined by the total number of files scanned

claims.claim: Scan cost is not determined by the number of classifiers.
claims.quote: Scan cost is determined by the total number of files scanned—not the number of classifiers.

claims.claim: Broader classifier selection can bring more files into scope.
claims.quote: Selecting a broader set of classifiers may increase the number of files in scope and raise overall cost.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to its pay-as-you-go pricing page for pricing.
claims.quote:
Understand pricing and estimate your expected monthly costs for pay-as-you-go capabilities:
Microsoft pay-as-you-go pricing

claims.claim: Trainable classifiers only work with unencrypted items.
claims.quote: Classifiers only work with items that aren't encrypted.

claims.claim: Custom trainable classifiers support English only.
claims.quote: Language limitation: Support for custom classifiers is limited to English.

claims.claim: Published custom classifiers cannot be retrained.
claims.quote: Retraining published custom classifiers isn't supported.

claims.claim: Improving a published classifier requires removing it and starting again with larger sample sets.
claims.quote: If you need to improve the accuracy of a trainable classifier you published, remove the classifier and start over with larger sample sets.

claims.where: Risks and limits: creator; What to check
claims.claim: By default only the creator can train a custom classifier and review its predictions.
claims.quote: By default, only the user who creates a custom classifier can train it and review predictions made by that classifier.

claims.claim: Training and testing seed files must be text-based, not images or image-only PDFs.
claims.quote: When seeding content for training or testing custom trainable classifiers, only text-based files are supported. You cannot use image files or image-only PDFs.

claims.claim: Selecting specific classifiers updates only their classification results.
claims.quote: If you select specific classifiers during a scan, only those classifiers have their classification results updated for the scanned files.

claims.claim: Other classifiers might remain unevaluated.
claims.quote: Other classifiers present in the files might remain unevaluated

claims.claim: Unevaluated classifiers might not trigger their associated policies.
claims.quote: Other classifiers present in the files might remain unevaluated and might not trigger their associated policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: actions on old files; Why it matters
claims.claim: A scan can trigger active policies on historical files, including sensitivity label application or removal.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, updated results can trigger active policies, including policies that apply or remove sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive scan processes up to 150,000 locations.
claims.quote:
Applies to SharePoint and OneDrive
Each scan can process up to 150,000 locations and 100 million files.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive scan processes up to 100 million files.
claims.quote: Each scan can process up to 150,000 locations and 100 million files.

claims.claim: Specific classifier selection is limited to 50 classifiers at a time.
claims.quote: If you choose to scan for specific classifiers, you can select up to 50 at a time.

claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive location in multiple active scans is successfully processed by only one.
claims.quote: If a location is in scope of multiple active scans, only one scan processes it successfully and marks it skipped for others.
